Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT)

Department of Allied Health Sciences

The Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) is a professional degree program designed to prepare graduates for careers in physical therapy, rehabilitation, and related healthcare services. The program provides a comprehensive foundation in basic medical sciences, human movement, clinical assessment, therapeutic interventions, and rehabilitation principles. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction with practical learning and clinical education to develop the knowledge, skills, and professional attitudes required for safe and effective physical therapy practice. Relevant areas of study include anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, pathology, therapeutic exercise, manual therapy, musculoskeletal rehabilitation, neurological rehabilitation, cardiopulmonary physical therapy, and other relevant disciplines. The program emphasizes the assessment of movement dysfunction, identification of physical impairments and functional limitations, development of individualized treatment plans, implementation of appropriate therapeutic interventions, and evaluation of rehabilitation outcomes. Students are also encouraged to develop critical thinking, communication, research literacy, ethical judgment, and interdisciplinary teamwork. Clinical education is an important component of professional preparation, enabling students to apply theoretical knowledge in supervised clinical settings and gain experience in managing patients with diverse rehabilitation needs. The program aims to prepare graduates for professional roles in hospitals, rehabilitation centers, physical therapy clinics, community healthcare settings, academic institutions, research, and other relevant healthcare environments, subject to applicable professional registration and employment requirements. Through its commitment to academic quality and professional development, the Department of Allied Health Sciences at the University of Loralai seeks to prepare competent, ethical, and compassionate physical therapy professionals who can contribute to the advancement of rehabilitation services and healthcare in Balochistan and across Pakistan.

BS Anesthesia Technology

Department of Allied Health Sciences

The Bachelor of Science in Anesthesia Technology (BS ANT) is an undergraduate allied health sciences program designed to prepare students for professional roles in anesthesia services, operating rooms, and perioperative healthcare settings. Anesthesia technology professionals support anesthesia teams by assisting with the preparation of equipment, checking anesthesia delivery systems, preparing monitoring devices, supporting airway management procedures, and contributing to patient monitoring and perioperative safety within their defined professional responsibilities. The program provides a foundation in basic medical sciences, including anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology, and other relevant clinical disciplines. Students also develop knowledge of anesthesia principles, anesthesia-related equipment, patient monitoring, airway management, infection prevention, emergency preparedness, and operating-room procedures. Practical education is an important component of the program. Through appropriate laboratory activities and supervised clinical placements, students develop familiarity with anesthesia equipment, clinical monitoring systems, patient safety practices, and the responsibilities of working within a multidisciplinary healthcare team. The program also emphasizes professional ethics, effective communication, critical thinking, research awareness, and evidence-based practice. These competencies help students understand their responsibilities, recognize clinical concerns, follow established protocols, and communicate effectively with qualified healthcare professionals. Graduates may pursue relevant employment opportunities in hospitals, surgical units, operating rooms, anesthesia departments, and other healthcare institutions offering anesthesia-related services, subject to applicable professional registration, employer requirements, and the graduate's authorized scope of practice. The Department of Allied Health Sciences at the University of Loralai aims to prepare competent, responsible, and safety-conscious anesthesia technology graduates who can contribute to quality perioperative care and the continued development of healthcare services in Balochistan and across Pakistan.

BS Optometry (BS OPT)

Department of Allied Health Sciences

The Bachelor of Science in Optometry (BS OPT) is an undergraduate allied health sciences program designed to prepare students for professional roles in vision assessment, refractive error management, and optometric care. Optometry focuses on the assessment of visual function, identification and correction of refractive errors, evaluation of ocular health, and recognition of conditions that may require referral to an ophthalmologist or another healthcare specialist. Optometry professionals contribute to the delivery of comprehensive eye care and help individuals maintain and improve their visual function. The program provides a foundation in basic medical sciences, including anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and pathology, alongside specialized subjects such as ocular anatomy and physiology, visual optics, geometric and physiological optics, refraction, clinical optometry, ocular diseases, contact lenses, binocular vision, and other relevant areas in accordance with the approved curriculum. Practical and clinical education is an essential component of optometry training. Through laboratory activities and supervised clinical placements, students develop skills in visual acuity assessment, refraction, use of optometric instruments, evaluation of visual function, and recognition of ocular abnormalities. Clinical learning also emphasizes patient communication, accurate record-keeping, professional ethics, infection prevention, and appropriate referral practices. The program further promotes research awareness, evidence-based practice, community eye health education, and lifelong professional development. These competencies help graduates respond to changing eye care needs and contribute to improved access to vision assessment and optometric services. Graduates may pursue relevant opportunities in optometry clinics, hospitals, eye care centers, optical practices, vision screening programs, community eye health initiatives, and academic or research settings, subject to applicable registration requirements, employer policies, and the graduate's authorized scope of practice. The Department of Allied Health Sciences at the University of Loralai aims to prepare competent, responsible, and patient-focused optometry graduates who can contribute to quality vision care and the development of eye health services in Balochistan and across Pakistan.

Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA)

Department of Management Sciences

The undergraduate business administration program, referred to as BBA/BSBA in departmental documentation, provides a broad foundation in business and management. It develops students' understanding of organizational functions, business environments, decision-making, and entrepreneurial opportunities. The curriculum covers major areas such as: • Principles of Management and Organizational Behavior • Accounting, Finance, and Economics • Marketing and Consumer Behavior • Human Resource Management • Business Statistics and Research Methods • Business Law and Taxation • Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management • International Business and E-Commerce • Management Information Systems • Corporate Ethics and Social Responsibility • Research Projects and relevant professional courses The program emphasizes practical application through projects, presentations, research activities, internships, and other learning opportunities in accordance with the approved scheme of studies.

Specialized Tracks
Human Resource Management (HRM)Finance & Banking
4 Years (8 Semesters)Overview
Undergraduate70 Credit Hrs

BS Business Administration (2.5-Year for Associate Degree Holders)

Department of Management Sciences

A specialized 2.5-year undergraduate program designed specifically for graduates holding 14-year Associate Degrees (ADA, ADS, ADC) or conventional BA, BSc, and B.Com qualifications. The curriculum features an intensive Semester IV bridging and deficiency component covering business mathematics, accounting, economics, ICT, and management principles, followed by advanced core courses, 6 specialization electives, an 8-week corporate internship, and a capstone BSBA project. Graduates earn a full 16-year equivalent BS Business Administration (BSBA / BBA) degree accredited by the Higher Education Commission (HEC), qualifying them for corporate leadership roles and direct postgraduate admission to MS Management Sciences and MBA programs.

Specialized Tracks
Human Resource Management (HRM)Banking & Corporate Finance
2.5 Years (5 Semesters)Overview
Graduate-4 Credit Hrs

MS in Management Sciences

Department of Management Sciences

The Master of Science (MS) in Management Sciences is a rigorous 2-year postgraduate research degree designed for graduates with 16 years of business education. The program structure comprises 30 to 36 total credit hours, balancing 12 credit hours of Core Graduate-level courses (Core-G), 12 credit hours of elective/specialization courses, and 6 credit hours of empirical thesis research. Students select from rich pools of advanced core disciplines and specialized concentration electives across Finance, Human Resource Management, and Marketing, cultivating high-impact quantitative and qualitative research competencies, managerial analytics, and scholarly contributions to organizational science.

Specialized Tracks
Finance & BankingHuman Resource Management (HRM)
